live_web_research.title: Anduril Acquires Popoto Modem to Scale Undersea Autonomous Networks
live_web_research.snippet: Anduril Industries has acquired Popoto Modem, a Massachusetts-based underwater acoustics firm, to expand multi-node mesh networking capabilities across its Copperhead autonomous underwater vehicle family and broader maritime systems portfolio.
live_web_research.page_text: Anduril Acquires Popoto Modem To Scale Undersea Autonomous Networks Skip to content Anduril Acquires Popoto Modem to Scale Undersea Autonomous Networks 7 October 2026 Edited By: Haley McQueen Anduril has announced the acquisition of Popoto Modem, an underwater acoustics company based in Massachusetts. (Image credit: Anduril) The future of maritime dominance hinges on the ability of a single operator to command dozens, even hundreds, of vehicles at once. That places a priority on persistent, resilient, and affordable communications infrastructure. That requirement, however, is complicated by the nuances of the undersea domain: sound waves are the only signal that travels a meaningful distance through water, making them the only way to transport the high-fidelity, low-latency data required to connect assets from surface to subsea. To make matters worse, undersea acoustic communications equipment has historically been prohibitively expensive, placing an upper limit on the size of undersea maritime formations. As a result, undersea communications are largely point-to-point links between expensive platforms—an architecture that doesn’t scale to the desired end state where a single operator can control many affordable autonomous systems. Popoto Modem’s acoustic communications technology changes that equation, enabling persistent, multi-node mesh networking underwater that lets autonomous vehicles communicate with each other, with surface vessels, and the broader fleet simultaneously. Anduril has worked with Popoto Modem for over a year, integrating their affordable acoustic modems into a variety of products across Anduril’s family of maritime systems. Acquiring Popoto Modem will accelerate Anduril’s efforts to develop, produce, and deploy a fleet of autonomous underwater systems. The immediate priority is scaling integrations into Anduril’s Copperhead family of affordable autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), enabling a single operator to command and oversee large formations of AUVs while maintaining confidence that every vehicle stays in contact and on task. Dominance of the undersea domain demands systems that operate together, rather than individually. That construct has underpinned Anduril’s work across every domain. Recently, at BlueTIDE 2026 and in the US Navy’s Lanternfish exercise, Anduril demonstrated how Lattice fuses disparate platforms above the waterline into a single operating picture, creating an integrated system to streamline port defense. Acquiring Popoto Modem enables Anduril to extend that integration to subsea, unlocking the affordable undersea communications mesh network required to deploy systems at scale. Popoto Modem brings flexible, agile acoustic hardware to the software and platforms Anduril has already built, allowing us to deliver more capable undersea systems to customers faster. live_web_research.page_text: Anduril acquires Popoto Modem to expand communications for autonomous underwater fleets Skip to content Anduril acquires Popoto Modem to expand communications for autonomous underwater fleets By Martin Chomsky (Defence Industry Europe) Corporate | October 3, 2026 Photo: Anduril Industries. Anduril Industries has acquired Popoto Modem, a Massachusetts-based underwater acoustics company, to expand communications across its autonomous maritime systems. The first priority is broader integration of Popoto’s technology into Anduril’s Copperhead autonomous underwater vehicle family. The acquisition follows more than a year of collaboration between the companies. During that period, Anduril integrated Popoto’s acoustic modems into several products across its maritime portfolio. Popoto’s technology enables multi-node acoustic mesh networks connecting underwater vehicles with each other, surface vessels and the broader fleet, according to Anduril. The company intends to use those connections to support large formations of autonomous systems under a single operator’s supervision. Anduril said traditional underwater communications equipment has been expensive, restricting the size of maritime formations. Existing arrangements largely rely on point-to-point links between individual platforms, which the company said do not scale adequately for larger fleets of affordable vehicles. Anduril plans to scale modem integration across the Copperhead family to help operators maintain contact with vehicles and oversee their missions. The acquisition brings Popoto’s acoustic hardware together with Anduril’s existing software and autonomous platforms. The company said this combination would accelerate the development, production and deployment of underwater systems. Its stated objective is to keep vehicles connected and on task while enabling one operator to manage larger formations. Anduril recently demonstrated its Lattice software at BlueTIDE 2026 and during the U.S. Navy’s Lanternfish exercise. Those demonstrations combined separate platforms above the waterline into a common operating picture for port defense. The company said Popoto’s technology would extend that integration to underwater systems. It identified affordable subsea mesh communications as a requirement for deploying autonomous maritime fleets at scale. Anduril Acquires Popoto Modem for Underwater Autonomous Networks

Anduril Industries has acquired Popoto Modem, a Massachusetts-based underwater acoustics firm, to expand multi-node mesh networking capabilities across its Copperhead autonomous underwater vehicle family and broader maritime systems portfolio. The acquisition follows over a year of collaboration between the companies, during which Anduril integrated Popoto's affordable acoustic modems into several products across its maritime portfolio. Popoto's technology enables multi-node acoustic mesh networks, allowing underwater vehicles to communicate with each other, with surface vessels, and the broader fleet. Anduril plans to scale modem integration across the Copperhead family to help operators maintain contact with vehicles and oversee their missions. The acquisition brings Popoto's acoustic hardware together with Anduril's existing software and autonomous platforms, accelerating the development, production, and deployment of underwater systems.
